title: Profile throughput-vs-quality Pareto for mixed batching and prefix-cache policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce an automated Pareto profile that maps throughput/latency against end-to-end output quality for mixed batching and prefix-cache configurations, and wire the results into regression monitoring and rollout decisions. This ticket focuses on systematic sweeps of microbatch size, batching timeout/window, prefix-cache TTL and chunking behavior, and simple KV cache eviction knobs. The output will be: (1) a canonical Pareto frontier visualization for our recommended workloads, (2) a small ruleset that recommends configs by SLO tier, and (3) a weekly job that re-runs the sweep and raises alerts when quality regressions cross thresholds for a given latency improvement.
motivation: We frequently tune batching and cache settings to reduce per-token cost and increase throughput. Past changes have occasionally produced subtle quality regressions (e.g., context truncation due to aggressive cache chunking, or stale prefix reuse). We need a repeatable profiling system that quantifies the tradeoffs and feeds our regression alerting and rollout guardrails.
metrics: Primary metrics: p50/p95 request latency (ms), tokens/sec (system-level), per-token cost estimate (USD/token), and quality measures computed on canonical eval suites: normalized log-likelihood delta (ΔNLL), average BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and a composite semantic similarity score (embedding cosine) against reference outputs. Detection thresholds: quality regression if ΔNLL > 0.25 or semantic similarity drop > 0.03 relative to baseline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pareto frontier plot generated for three representative workloads (short chat, long completion, instruction-following) covering at least 12 configuration points each. 2) A table mapping SLO tiers (latency/p50 targets) to recommended config sets. 3) Automation: a scheduled pipeline in CI that runs the sweep weekly and posts summarized results to the Console dashboard + a webhook to the regression monitor. 4) A documented playbook describing how to interpret wins (latency gain with quality within tolerance) vs. unsafe regressions. 5) One PR that wires the recommended default config into runtime-1.22 feature flags behind a canary rollout policy.
run_plan: Step 1: finalise canonical eval set (use eval-suite v2026-02 + 3 new long-form threads). Step 2: implement harness that can deploy combinations of: microbatch sizes (1,2,4,8), batching time windows (5ms,20ms,50ms,100ms), prefix-cache TTLs (0s,5s,30s,120s), and chunk-sizes (32,64,128 tokens). Step 3: run sweeps on a dedicated cluster with fixed seed traffic replay and measure latency and quality. Step 4: compute Pareto frontier and flag configurations dominated by both lower latency and higher quality. Step 5: commit visualization + generated recommendations and schedule weekly re-run. Step 6: add alerts (PagerDuty/Slack) for regressions exceeding thresholds.
datasets_and_artifacts: Eval suite: latency-quality-regression-set-v4 (public examples + curated customer prompts). Baseline model: redwood-open-3b@v2026-02. Artifacts will be stored in: Console dashboard (dashboard id: perf/pareto/40821), S3 folder s3://redwood-evals/pareto/ENG-40821/, and a GitHub PR with harness code (will link below).
initial_findings: Early partial sweep (microbatch and TTL only) shows that increasing microbatch from 1->4 improves tokens/sec by ~40% with p95 latency regressions only for long sequences; prefix-cache TTL trades off minor latency improvement for occasional context mismatch on instruction-chat traces. These results motivate a more granular sweep of cache chunk-size and eviction policy. No safety or security issues identified so far.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: batching/caching combos could produce silent quality regression not captured by automated metrics. Mitigation: include a stratified human evaluation on borderline configs and conservative rollout (canary with auto-fallback). Risk: noisy measurement due to infra variance; mitigation: run each config for 30 minutes under replayed traffic and use median of 3 runs.
next_steps: 1) Finish implementation of chunk-size sweep and run full-perf sweep (owner: Liam). 2) Create PR that adds scheduled job and dashboard panels (owner: Aisha). 3) Draft playbook for SRE on how to respond to regression alerts and rollback (owner: SRE lead). Target to merge runtime-1.22 flag PR by 2026-03-20.

owner_notes: Aim to keep the profiling light-weight and reproducible. If we see a clear config that yields >=25% throughput improvement without quality loss, propose it as default for non-enterprise tenants behind a runtime flag. For enterprise tenants with strict SLAs, keep conservative defaults and expose recommendations in Console.
